display_name: Lift Codex Stage1 Summaries Into Ledger
description:
One-shot operator-only rewrite of `session_ledger__session.summary_text` from Codex `stage1_outputs.rollout_summary`. Joins Codex's stage1 phase-2 candidate set (filtered to `selected_for_phase2 = 1` — the canonical-input subset the Codex phase-2 algorithm operates on) to existing `__session` rows by `external_session_id = thread_id`, then rewrites each match's `summary_text` to the stage1 `rollout_summary` with `internal:auto_summarize:codex_stage1_seed` attribution on the chunk push.

Why this verb exists. When Codex's stage1 pipeline produces a higher-quality session summary than M6's auto-summarize cron arrived at, the ledger's denormalized `summary_text` (and its embedding) needs a one-shot upgrade. The verb routes the stage1 text through `push_summary_chunk` so the embedding regenerates against the better summary, then the operator's `search_sessions` semantic search returns the stage1-quality hit.

Flow. The verb wraps the per-row lift in a try/finally pause-resume envelope around the M6 SUMMARIZE cron (NOT the poll cron): (1) `scheduling_service.clear_scheduled_actions_by_tag(tag)` pauses M6 so a concurrent auto-summarize firing can't race the rewrite; (2) per candidate row in ONE transaction: SELECT FOR UPDATE the `__session` row, UPDATE `summary_text` to `rollout_summary`, DELETE the stale `__summary` `chunk_index = 0` row to avoid UPSERT-vs-INSERT-OR-FAIL ambiguity, then `push_summary_chunk` for fresh embedding generation; (3) the `finally` block calls `ensure_periodic_summarize_schedule(cadence_minutes, tag)` so the M6 cron resumes even when the per-row loop raises.

Idempotent. Re-running after a successful lift is a no-op because the second pass sees `summary_text` already equals `rollout_summary` (UPDATE writes the same value; DELETE + `push_summary_chunk` regenerates the embedding harmlessly). Safe to re-run for partial recovery.

Default `confirm=False` returns a structured dry-run carrying `stage1_row_count` (rows in `stage1_outputs` matching `selected_for_phase2 = 1`) + `candidate_count` (subset of stage1 rows that match an existing `__session` row by `external_session_id = thread_id`). Pass `confirm=true` to actually rewrite.

This verb is `is_discoverable=False` — the model cannot find it via process_search and never proposes it. Operator-only via the operator bridge.
embedding_description: Operator-only one-shot: rewrite __session.summary_text from Codex stage1_outputs.rollout_summary for sessions whose external_session_id matches a stage1 thread_id (selected_for_phase2=1). Routes through push_summary_chunk for fresh embedding. Pauses M6 SUMMARIZE cron, per-row SELECT FOR UPDATE + UPDATE + DELETE-stale-chunk + push, resumes cron in finally. Default dry-run; confirm=true to commit.

result_processor_customizations.action_label: Lift Codex Stage1 Summaries Into Ledger
result_processor_customizations.result_description: Codex stage1 lift outcome. `confirmed=false` is a dry-run; `confirmed=true` ran the per-row rewrite. `stage1_row_count` is the rows considered in `stage1_outputs` (selected_for_phase2 = 1). `candidate_count` is the subset that matched an existing `__session` row by `external_session_id = thread_id`. `lifted_count` is the sessions actually rewritten this call (always 0 on dry-run).
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: After a confirmed lift, re-run with `confirm=False` to verify `lifted_count` from the prior call matches the new `candidate_count` (idempotent re-run). Then call `search_sessions` with a query that previously surfaced the M6-auto-summarized session; confirm the new envelope's summary_text matches the stage1 rollout_summary. If `candidate_count` is surprisingly low relative to `stage1_row_count`, the gap is stage1 thread_ids that don't match any ledger external_session_id — likely Codex sessions that never landed in the ledger (cursor offset, source disabled, etc).

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Pause-and-rewrite pass over `__session.summary_text` from Codex stage1_outputs; pauses M6 SUMMARIZE cron, per-row SELECT FOR UPDATE + UPDATE + DELETE-stale-chunk + push_summary_chunk transaction, resumes cron in finally-block
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: LedgerRepositoryError: the underlying state_service rejected one of the per-session UPDATE / DELETE / chunk-push operations OR the pause/resume scheduling call failed. If scheduling_service was None, the verb fails fast before the lift loop. If the M6 embedding_service / vector_service bindings are missing on this profile, push_summary_chunk raises SummaryServicesUnavailableError mid-loop and the finally-block still re-ensures the cron. Possible causes: schema not yet initialized, state_service unavailable, scheduling_service unbound on this profile, M6 services unbound, Codex stage1 sqlite file inaccessible.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Confirm scheduling_service + embedding_service + vector_service are all bound (per-profile). Confirm Codex's stage1 sqlite path is readable (default `~/.codex/memories_1.sqlite`). Confirm schema is initialized via `list_sources`. The finally-block re-ensures the M6 SUMMARIZE cron even on exception; if the verb itself raised before the pause call, the cron was never paused and is still running. If a specific session repeatedly fails the per-row transaction (visible via log lines), inspect via `get_session_timeline` for an oversized rollout_summary or malformed content.
